design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to either the intervention group or the control group using computer-generated random numbers with stratified randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, stratified, and concealed by an independent research assistant until after recruitment and baseline testing.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A random assignment stratified by age, existence of family history or friends with cancer; and educational level, was carried out. Random numbers generated by computer were employed... The research assistant, who had no contact with the participants, generated the random assignment sequence, and assigned the participants (recruited by the researchers) to one or other group. This method ensured blinding up to the point when interventions were assigned.

domain_judgments.rationale: Neither participants nor interviewers administering the intervention were blinded, and the analysis excluded participants who were lost to follow-up (complete case analysis rather than full ITT).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The participants and the researchers administering the intervention had knowledge of the group to which each participant had been assigned... Adherence to the information protocol during the study was ensured by monitoring the content of the informative document... Numbers of women assigned to the standard information (control) and experimental information (intervention) groups were 216 and 218, respectively. Of these totals, 178 of the control and 177 of the IG were included in the analyses

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was around 18% in both groups (40/218 in control, 39/216 in intervention), balanced between arms, with reasons unrelated to the trial interventions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the second round of interviews, 355 women were interviewed by telephone... Assigned to standard information control group n = 218... Non-response to the 2nd survey 1 month later n = 40... Assigned to experimental info intervention group n = 216... Non-response to the 2nd survey 1 month later n = 39

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were self-reported via telephone interview where participants were not blinded to their assigned condition and it is not specified whether telephone interviewers were blinded to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: One month after the first interview the second was carried out, by telephone, with the object of evaluating again their knowledge, attitudes, decision, anxiety/depression and fear of cancer... The knowledge analysis questionnaire was adapted from a questionnaire developed by the Health Decision Group... The questionnaire had four multiple-choice questions, each with three possible answers, scoring 1 point each, and three free-response questions, each with one possible answer, scoring 2 points each.

domain_judgments.rationale: While the trial was registered, secondary scales such as the Cancer Worry Scale were added mid-study and multiple analyses (both continuous score and dichotomized cutoff) were reported without a detailed prespecified analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was registered (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT01335906) in April 2011... The analysis of worries about cancer was performed with only 62 control and 59 IG participants, because this scale was introduced in the study some time after it had been initiated.

overall_summary: The trial had sound computer-generated stratified randomization with central allocation concealment; however, lack of participant/assessor blinding during telephone follow-up interviews and modifications to secondary outcome assessments during the trial raise some concerns.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly selected and assigned to receive either the new or old information leaflet using a computer-assisted random procedure.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-assisted random sequence was used and allocation was concealed from practices and participants via pseudonyms on envelopes, with balanced baseline characteristics between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The 24 participants from each practice were selected by a computer-assisted random procedure, and the group allotment process was also random. The authors wrote each participant's pseudonym on the envelope that she was to receive, and the practices put the actual names and addresses on the envelopes and sent them. The participants and their family physicians were blinded with respect to group allotment, but the study team was not.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were blinded to which leaflet was the 'old' or 'new' version, the intervention was delivered as mailed materials without protocol deviations, and analysis adhered to assigned groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The participants and their family physicians were blinded with respect to group allotment, but the study team was not. The participants were asked by letter to fill out the questionnaire after reading the leaflet and to send it back in an envelope that was also enclosed in the mailing.

domain_judgments.rationale: Over 53% of participants in each group did not return questionnaires, creating substantial missing outcome data that could plausibly be related to participants' interest and attitudes toward screening.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 185 questionnaires were filled out and returned by each of the two groups (response rate, 46.7%); it was coincidental that this number was the same in both groups. 178 questionnaires from group A and 175 from group B were evaluable (total, 353; see Figure 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were assessed identically in both groups using self-administered questionnaires, and participants were unaware of study hypotheses or which leaflet was novel.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint was the yes-or-no question whether the participant would decide to undergo screening if invited to do so right now, at the time of questioning (eTable 2).

domain_judgments.rationale: The study had a prospective registration and published protocol, and outcomes and primary analyses were reported in accordance with the pre-specified plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study was approved by the Ethics Committee of the Universitätsklinikum Düsseldorf (University Hospital Düsseldorf) on 22 February 2012 (study no. 3797) and was registered with TRIALS (DRKS00004271)... In accordance with the protocol, group differences in the primary endpoint “willingness to participate: yes/no” were tested for significance using the likelihood ratio chi-square test with a two-tailed α of 5% (non-directional hypothesis).

overall_summary: The study is at high overall risk of bias due to substantial missing outcome data (response rate under 47%, with over 53% attrition in both randomized groups). All other RoB 2 domains demonstrated low risk of bias.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to the intervention (leaflet) or control condition (no leaflet) using computer-generated random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated via computer random numbers, baseline characteristics between groups were balanced, and there is no indication of allocation concealment failure.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Women who provided consent and their e-mail address were randomised to the intervention condition (leaflet) or the control condition (no leaflet) by computer-generated random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants in this educational intervention could not be blinded, but the online delivery adhered to the intended protocol and analyses reflect the assigned groups without substantial non-protocol interventions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two weeks after completing their first questionnaire, participants in the intervention group were asked to read an online information leaflet (see below). Participants in the control condition did not receive this leaflet.

domain_judgments.rationale: While follow-up survey completion was relatively high for questionnaire outcomes (988/1312, 75%), nearly half the sample had missing data for the priming task outcome, with documented demographic differences between completers and non-completers.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A weakness of this study was that only about half of the participants completed the priming task. This reduced the power of the analyses and could have led to selection bias. Comparing demographics, the participants who completed the priming task were more often higher educated, less often retired, and more often first-time invitees than the participants who did not complete the priming task.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were assessed through validated computerized tasks and questionnaires, as well as objective registry data for screening attendance, with identical measurement across study arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Screening knowledge, explicit attitudes, and implicit associations were assessed through web-based questionnaires, at baseline and two weeks later. Actual screening attendance data were collected.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective clinical trial registry number or pre-analysis plan was cited, and post-hoc data exclusion choices were made regarding implicit association task items.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Due to misconceptions regarding one of the targets (double meaning in Dutch) the response times for this target were excluded for analyses.

overall_summary: The study had overall some concerns due to substantial missing data for the implicit association priming task (with demonstrated differences between completers and non-completers) and the lack of a pre-registered trial analysis protocol combined with post-hoc exclusions of target words.

design_rationale: The study is a parallel two-stage cluster randomized controlled trial where 40 Basic Health Areas (BHAs) were randomized to intervention or control using computer-generated blocks, and random samples of women within each BHA were invited.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated by an independent statistician using computer-generated blocks stratified by socioeconomic level, and baseline characteristics were broadly balanced across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the first stage, elementary territorial units of the healthcare system named Basic Health Areas (BHAs) were stratified by socioeconomic level [14] and 40 of them were selected and randomised to intervention or control using computer-generated blocks of size two. In the second stage, random samples of 30 to 50 women within each BHA were obtained. ... The random allocation sequence was generated by a statistician with no contact with the participants (MR).

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding of participants to educational/informational intervention materials is impossible, and analysis was restricted to complete cases rather than a full intention-to-treat approach, though there were no obvious non-protocol deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trained interviewers, not aware of the women's allocation, contacted them by phone, briefly described the study and determined eligibility. ... The main analysis included all women that had completed the pre- and post-intervention questionnaires with no missing data. Missing values imputation was not done in women lost to follow-up or who had not completed the post-intervention questionnaire.

domain_judgments.rationale: Post-baseline retention was high and balanced between groups (203/260 [78.1%] vs 197/264 [74.6%]), and sensitivity analyses confirmed that missing data did not meaningfully impact baseline balance or the primary outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The baseline questionnaire was completed by 524 women (49.2% of the invited and eligible), 260 and 264 women in the intervention and control groups, respectively. The post-intervention questionnaire was completed by 400 women, 203 in the intervention group and 197 in the control group, which represents a response rate of 37.6% among the invited and eligible women. ... The sensitivity analysis showed no differences with the complete case analysis in terms of baseline characteristics comparability or primary outcome.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were measured via self-administered web questionnaires or interviewers unaware of allocation using validated scales, but the subjective self-reported nature of knowledge and attitudes in an unblinded trial introduces some risk of bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was informed choice about breast cancer screening, a dichotomous outcome defined as adequate knowledge and intentions consistent with attitudes... Most of the outcome measures were obtained through validated scales that have shown suitability in previous studies. ... Trained interviewers, not aware of the women's allocation, contacted them by phone... 305 of which responded via web.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was registered prior to completion of analysis (NCT03046004) and followed a pre-specified published protocol with pre-defined primary and secondary endpoints.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The InforMa study was registered with the ClinicalTrials.gov registry, number NCT03046004. ... We performed the statistical analysis as planned in the protocol [14].

overall_summary: The study has some concerns overall due to participant awareness of intervention materials affecting self-reported outcomes and a complete-case analysis, despite robust cluster randomization and pre-specified protocol endpoints.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to the intervention or control decision aid using a computer-generated random sequence with permuted blocks.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, concealed until after recruitment, and baseline characteristics were balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A programmer who had no contact with participants generated the randomisation sequence using a computer system that was inaccessible until after recruitment; therefore, interviewers were unaware of the materials that women would receive (ensuring allocation concealment). We assigned participants to either the intervention or control group in a 1:1 ratio with permuted block sizes of four and eight.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were blinded to which version was the experimental intervention, the booklet intervention was delivered via mail with no substantial opportunity for trial-context deviations, and analysis followed an intention-to-treat approach supported by sensitivity analyses with multiple imputation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Women knew they would receive one of two versions of an information booklet but did not know how these differed or which one was the intervention. ... In accordance with our published protocol, we included in our primary analysis all participants as randomised, except for those lost to follow-up and those for whom some outcome data were missing because of incomplete answers to the telephone questionnaire

domain_judgments.rationale: Missing outcome data accounted for less than 8% overall, were very balanced between study arms, and sensitivity analyses imputing missing data yielded consistent results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 21 women in the intervention group and 20 controls were lost to follow-up; a further ten women assigned to the intervention and 11 controls did not answer all questions on attitudes. Therefore, 409 women in the intervention group and 408 controls were analysed for the primary outcome.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were measured using standardized validated structured interview scales administered identically across arms by interviewers blinded to allocation until the final question.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We designed the follow-up interview to ensure the group assignment was unclear to the interviewer until the final question. Researchers who analysed data were unaware of the random allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered with a published protocol, and results were analyzed and reported in line with the prespecified analysis plan and outcome definitions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was informed choice (defined as adequate knowledge and consistency between attitudes and screening intentions)... This trial is registered with the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry, number ACTRN12613001035718. ... In accordance with our published protocol, we included in our primary analysis all participants as randomised

overall_summary: This randomized trial used robust computer-generated allocation concealment, effective blinding of participants and outcome assessors, experienced low attrition balanced across groups, and followed a prespecified protocol and analysis plan. Consequently, all RoB 2 domains were judged to have low risk of bias.
